prompt: A responsive web analytics dashboard has been implemented from an approved visual direction. Perform visual verification in the real browser at 1440x900, 900x900, and 390x844 CSS-pixel viewports in both light and dark themes. Exercise loading, empty, normal, and dense-data states; the dense state uses 48-character card titles and the maximum supported badge count. Verify hierarchy, card alignment, spacing consistency, wrapping/truncation, chart and legend clipping, horizontal overflow, sticky-header overlap, and whether the primary action remains visually distinct. Hold browser version, DPR, fonts, dataset, and animation state constant for comparable captures. Record every failed claim against a capture and distinguish meaningful layout drift from rendering noise.

requirements: approved reference captures are supplied for the default desktop state only
the browser harness can force viewport, theme, deterministic data, disabled animations, and the bundled production fonts
loading, empty, normal, and dense states are reachable without changing application code
the implementation declares 390 CSS pixels as its narrowest supported browser width

falsifiableChecks.assertion: Captures exist for all required viewport/theme combinations and include the loading, empty, normal, and dense states needed to test the stated claims.

No supported state has unintended horizontal overflow, chart/legend clipping, sticky-header overlap, or unreadable title/badge collision; any observed failure is tied to its exact capture and environment.
The primary action and content hierarchy remain visually legible across widths/themes, and screenshot differences are interpreted only after fonts, DPR, animation, data, and runtime are stabilized.

evidence: capture matrix targets plausible visual failure modes instead of arbitrary screenshot volume
hierarchy and spacing judgments are grounded in the implemented visual direction
rendering noise is not mislabeled as product drift

requiredEvidence: explicit unavailable or simulated evidence labels
